title: [WT-13] Wrappers: control checkout follows the target; QA reviews landed bytes
description:
Plan against docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md §6.

Objective: seats keep running the wrapper from committed main bytes. The control checkout sits on its own branch, moe/control, and fast-forwards to the target after every landing, so HEAD and the working files always move together and task-5998f871's committed-bytes reload is never deferred forever. QA only reviews a task whose landed commit the control checkout contains.

Deliverable, in scripts/moe-agent.sh and scripts/moe-agent.ps1 as twins:
- follow_control_checkout / Invoke-MoeControlFollow runs `git -C <control> -c core.hooksPath=<empty dir> merge --ff-only refs/heads/<target>`:
  - after L12 (L13);
  - at every loop top BEFORE the hot-reload check (wrapper_reload_deferred / Test-MoeWrapperReloadDeferred from task-5998f871e03d4ed5ab21f214073d85b2);
  - in the QA pre-flight after the claim.
- Branch states:
  - On the target or detached at the same commit: switch to moe/control, created at that commit if missing.
  - On another branch: MOE_CONTROL_NOT_FOLLOWING, no follow, one #general alert per hour.
  - A refused ff (local edits): MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_BEHIND, with git's file list and an hourly alert.
  - moe/control ahead of the target: MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_DIVERGED, alert; it is never reset.
  - Success: MOE_CONTROL_ADVANCED.
  - A follow failure never fails a landing.
- QA pre-flight: if the task's completion sha is not an ancestor of the control's HEAD after the follow, print MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_BEHIND, launch no CLI and call report_blocked.
- A wrapper whose own path is under <git top>/.worktrees/ refuses to start with MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE.
- Cases in scripts/tests/postflight.sh and postflight.ps1. Depends on WT-12 (task-06910296f63b4868849dc46cbb38a731) and task-5998f871.

NOT in scope: daemon dist rebuilds or restarts; worktree removal (WT-14); the §7.3 runbook text (WT-16); docs (WT-18).

Verification: node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash && bash scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh (and on a Windows seat: node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs powershell)
definitionOfDone: postflight case (both harnesses): after a worktree landing, the control checkout on moe/control has HEAD == target and a clean `git status -- scripts/` (the wrapper file on disk equals HEAD's blob), and MOE_CONTROL_ADVANCED is printed.
postflight case: with a changed scripts/moe-agent.sh landed on the target, the next loop top follows first and the hot-reload check sees no uncommitted wrapper edit (no deferral line).

postflight cases: control on main at the target commit switches to moe/control; on another branch prints MOE_CONTROL_NOT_FOLLOWING; a local edit to a landed file prints MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_BEHIND; a local commit on moe/control prints MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_DIVERGED and is not reset.

postflight case: a QA claim whose completion sha is not in the control HEAD prints MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_BEHIND, launches no CLI and calls report_blocked; a wrapper started from .worktrees/<id>/scripts/ prints MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE and exits non-zero.
Existing postflight and worktree-landing cases pass unchanged; both wrappers carry the same MOE_WORKTREE_/MOE_LAND_/MOE_CONTROL_/MOE_BOARD_ codes; the verification command exits 0.

implementationPlan.description: 1. Reject execution of wrappers from task worktrees (tests first). Goal: seats use committed control-checkout wrapper bytes; normal shared launches and bundled non-Git wrappers remain unchanged. Architecture: startup guard on wrapper identity; control-follow only in worktree operation; QA checks the served completion after follow. Tech: Git/Bash/Python and PS5.1. Read revised design §6 and landed WT-12/WT-04 mode/target seams; do not reimplement them. Add a guard before daemon/config/claim side effects using the actual wrapper source path (BASH_SOURCE / PSCommandPath), not current cwd, --project or MOE_WORKTREE_PATH. Canonicalize source and its own Git checkout/common repository location; if the source is inside that repository's reserved .worktrees/<id>/ subtree, including a linked-worktree root or symlink/junction alias, print MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE and exit nonzero. Distinguish a real path-component descendant from names like .worktrees-other; do not reject an unrelated project merely because an ancestor elsewhere has that spelling. Non-Git bundled wrapper is not falsely treated as a task worktree. Use argument arrays/literal paths and the existing Windows/WSL normalization with ordinal comparisons, preserving POSIX case. Twin cases: actual registered task worktree wrapper refuses even with --project control or cwd outside W; symlink alias where supported; control and non-Git bundled wrapper still launch; path with spaces; assert zero claim/daemon-start/CLI calls on refusal.

2. Implement follow_control_checkout / Invoke-MoeControlFollow with non-destructive branch handling and error handling. These are NEW twin helpers. Use explicit control root/target and local Git variables so worktree landing globals are not overwritten. Enable from the effective worktree mode (project mode for control seats, pinned mode for a worker attempt); shared attempts stay on their existing path. Resolve target using the landed literal consolidationBranch-or-main rule. Read HEAD and target as commits and symbolic branch. On refs/heads/moe/control proceed. On the target branch, or detached HEAD exactly at target, create moe/control at that same HEAD using hooks-off git switch -c if absent, or switch to it only if its existing tip equals current HEAD; never -C/-f, never reuse a different existing tip. On another branch or switch failure print MOE_CONTROL_NOT_FOLLOWING and leave every ref/file unchanged. For moe/control, require `git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD refs/heads/<target>`: exit 1 (ahead OR diverged) gives MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_DIVERGED, other errors refuse without guessing. Equal tips are an idempotent no-op. Before advancing ensure the proposed ff does not change .moe paths; runtime state must remain daemon-owned. Run exactly `git -C <control> -c core.hooksPath=<owned empty dir> merge --ff-only refs/heads/<target>`. Success with HEAD movement prints MOE_CONTROL_ADVANCED; failure prints MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_BEHIND plus bounded Git stderr/file list. Never reset, stash, force, delete a lock, stage board files or clean human dirt. Re-read HEAD after contention so a peer's completed follow can count as an already-current no-op, not false divergence. Twin tests: main->new/existing-same moe/control, detached-at-target, ordinary ff with HEAD==target and disk script==HEAD blob, already-current, unrelated branch, mismatched existing moe/control, ahead/diverged control, conflicting local edit/untracked file, Git-lock/refusal and dirty .moe sentinels preserved. A failure must not modify the published target.

3. Wire all follow sites and bounded operator alerts. Invoke the helper (a) after successful completion L12 as L13, (b) at every loop top after polling and BEFORE wrapper hash/committed-byte reload checks, including first iteration, (c) after a QA claim/context fetch before launch. Ensure initial loop follow/auto-switch happens before WT-04's worker moe/control prerequisite check; a human feature branch remains WT-04's report_blocked/no-W path. Preserve wrapper_reload_deferred/Test-MoeWrapperReloadDeferred, syntax checks, deferred-hash logic and reload/deregister flow unchanged, including Bash's grouped-loop exit fence. L13 failure is warning-only and cannot alter C's committed/landed outcome or re-finalize it as failed. For NOT_FOLLOWING/BEHIND/DIVERGED, send one #general alert per hour across seats of this control checkout, naming root/target/code and preserving Git's useful path list without unbounded output. Keep shared throttle state under the common Git directory, not .moe; a small exclusive-create/mkdir guard around read/update of a UTC-epoch timestamp is sufficient. Concurrent callers skip a held alert lock; notification/metadata failure never blocks follow or landing, and cleanup is in finally. No sleeping/spinning on another seat. Test the L13 result stays landed under follow refusal; two callers/repeated loop warnings generate at most one chat row inside an hour, then another after a fixture-adjusted timestamp (no real hour sleep); hooks never run during switch/ff. Add a committed target-only wrapper change to the existing reload scratch fixture: next loop follows before hash comparison, source equals HEAD and no MOE_WRAPPER_RELOAD_DEFERRED appears; unchanged shared reload cases still pass.

4. Gate QA launch on the actual recorded completion's ancestry. Read `task.landing.lastCompletion.sha` from the claimed task's served context (verified getContext.ts buildLanding field), not a checkpoint, rescue SHA, task branch tip or arbitrary HEAD. After control follow, validate it as a commit and run `git -C <control> merge-base --is-ancestor <completionSha> HEAD`. Exit 0 permits QA, including a later target containing C; absent/invalid/unavailable SHA or nonzero Git result prints MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_BEHIND with the task/SHA/reason, launches no CLI and calls report_blocked for that claimed task. Use the existing preflight-block path and identity; on RPC failure still do not launch or fall through to taskless QA, and report the failed acknowledgement. Leave actual task status/ownership changes to Moe. In the worktree QA prompt name the review commit and `git diff <sha>^ <sha>` so a later HEAD is not mistaken for this task's diff. Do not change shared-mode QA behavior. Add a conditional lastCompletion projection to the ONE shared postflight-fake-proxy.js using explicit test fixture input/task record; unset remains today's payload and no production daemon edit is needed. Twin tests: C absent while follow is refused -> code, exactly one report_blocked and no fake CLI; C becomes ancestor after ff -> launch; C is an ancestor of later HEAD -> launch; malformed/missing SHA and Git error -> no launch; task checkpoint must not satisfy the check; shared fixture unchanged.

5. Run the one focused verification gate. Exact root command: `node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash && bash scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh`. Expect exit 0, safe-harness failureClass NONE, all existing/added postflight cases and unchanged held-out worktree-landing local/remote cases passing, parity PASS. On the native Windows seat run `node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs powershell` and `powershell -NoProfile -File scripts/tests/worktree-landing.ps1` against the same bytes; preserve PS5.1 coverage and do not label missing-engine/skipped checks as passed. Compare held-out tests to WT-08T landed SHA with git diff --quiet and compare sorted code-family tokens MOE_(WORKTREE|LAND|CONTROL|BOARD)_ across both wrappers. Assert git status -- scripts/ clean in the successful scratch-control fixture, script disk bytes equal the HEAD blob, original control dirt unchanged in refusal fixtures, and no .moe runtime file written through W. Save fresh command/exitCode/outputTail for complete_task. No daemon rebuild/restart, cleanup/sweep, migration runbook, IDE or whole-system regression work in this slice.

6. Final adversarial self-review then QA handoff. Load adversarial-self-review and review this diff once for two seats following concurrently, a human switching branches or editing while follow runs, ahead versus diverged ancestry, target checked out elsewhere, control branch name collision, alias/case/path-boundary bypass of the wrapper guard, clock/alert-lock failures, and QA checking a rescue/checkpoint rather than the recorded completion. Confirm only moe/control HEAD/worktree advance by ff; target/main is never updated here; human dirt and daemon .moe are never discarded; a landing already recorded cannot become failed; follow precedes hot-reload and WT-04 checks. Preserve existing loop/parser/reload behavior and held-out tests. Keep ≤400 net non-board LOC through small helpers and table-driven cases. Correct defects within five declared files and rerun the named gate if bytes change. Record all actual modifiedFiles, complete via moe.complete_task with fresh evidence, write handoff; no agent Git staging/commit. WT-14 owns removal, WT-16/18 docs, WT-19 whole-epic hardening.

comments.author: worker-0062feec
comments.content:
Spike self-review correction for rail 4 (docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md §6.1, §6.2, §6.4, §6.5; section numbers unchanged). Where this differs from the description, this comment wins.

1. The follow runs in three places only:
   - at L13;
   - in a worker or QA pre-flight, after a claim whose workspace.mode is `worktree`;
   - at the loop top, but ONLY while HEAD is refs/heads/moe/control.
   A loop top on any other branch does nothing: no follow, no switch, no MOE_CONTROL_NOT_FOLLOWING alert. In shared mode that branch is moe/work-<date>, or main in a main-direct project. Add a case: a loop top on moe/work-<date> prints no MOE_CONTROL_ code and leaves HEAD alone.
2. So the auto-switch and the NOT_FOLLOWING alert happen only after a worktree-mode claim or at L13. Your DoD cases "control on main switches" and "another branch prints NOT_FOLLOWING" run after such a claim.
3. MOE_CONTROL_ADVANCED <old>..<new> is printed when the follow moves HEAD.
4. In remote mode, the QA pre-flight runs sync_land_target (L4's fetch and mirror) before the follow, so a commit landed from another clone is in the control checkout's HEAD.
5. MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE fires only inside <git top>/.worktrees/task-*. The using-git-worktrees skill and humans keep their own worktrees under .worktrees/, and two such directories exist today.

comments.author: worker-0062feec
comments.content:
Correction to my comment e6073e9d, points 1 and 2 (design doc §6.2/§6.5/§7.2 updated to match). A QA or architect claim always records workspace.mode 'shared' (WT-01's contract), so the QA pre-flight cannot gate on its claim.

- The follow runs:
  - at L13;
  - in a WORKER pre-flight after a claim whose workspace.mode is 'worktree' (the only place the auto-switch and MOE_CONTROL_NOT_FOLLOWING can fire);
  - in the QA pre-flight and at every loop top, only while the control checkout is in worktree mode, i.e. HEAD is exactly refs/heads/moe/control.
- Reuse WT-07's predicate, sh control_worktree_mode / ps1 Test-MoeControlWorktreeMode (Serena decision-worktree-control-seat-mode-signal, #general msg-46da6ff7). Any git failure counts as shared.
- For a control seat, a HEAD off moe/control means shared mode: nothing runs and nothing alerts (rail 4).
- Points 3-5 stand.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Use native hooks-off git switch and merge --ff-only on moe/control, no ref-only writes/reset/stash/index surgery. Keep the landed committed-bytes hot reload implementation unchanged and invoke follow immediately before it. Reuse common-gitdir metadata for cross-seat alert throttling and the existing shared fake proxy for QA context.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Verified wrapper_reload_deferred/Test-MoeWrapperReloadDeferred and their loop-top hash checks; Bash now groups its loop and exit to prevent stale-offset parsing (f31d415d in-flight bytes visible). Preserve that structure and hot-reload deregistration/parse logic. getContext.ts buildLanding exposes task.landing.lastCompletion.sha; current fake get_context omits it, so tests need a conditional fixture projection (fifth file). No existing control-follow or hourly-alert helper was found.
planningNotes.risks: Simultaneous control follows may lose Git locks; treat refusal as warning without retry spins or index.lock deletion. Never switch to an existing moe/control at a different commit, force a branch, overwrite human dirt or change target refs. Canonicalize the wrapper's OWN path independently of the supplied project/cwd, including Windows/WSL spellings and symlink aliases. QA ancestry proves the landed commit is contained, not that current HEAD equals it; the review diff remains C^..C.
